terms.name: exact_g1
terms.title: Exact G1 twins
terms.summary: The contiguous bars have the same global price ordering and ties as the selected Composer drawing.
formula: Rank all low, body low, body high and high endpoints across the window together.
Every corresponding rank matches, including ties. In oriented mode every body direction also matches.

terms.name: chained_g1
terms.title: Chained G1 twins
terms.summary: The contiguous bars, read as a chain, have the same global price ordering and ties as the selected Composer drawing.
formula: Read the first bar of the window as recorded.
Read every later bar as opening at the close of the recorded bar just before it; its low and high widen to include that open, and its direction follows from that open.
Rank all low, body low, body high and high endpoints across the window together.
Every corresponding rank matches, including ties. In oriented mode every body direction also matches.
A one-bar window has no later bar, so it reads exactly as exact_g1 reads it.

terms.name: wick_rejection
terms.title: Wick rejection
terms.summary: A bar whose small body sits at the top of its range after a long lower wick (rejection of lower prices).
formula: range = high − low; the event needs range > 0
body = |close − open|
lower_wick = min(open, close) − low
event ⇔ range > 0 ∧ body ≤ body_max × range ∧ lower_wick ≥ wick_min × range

terms.name: channel_breakout
terms.title: Channel breakout
terms.summary: The trigger bar closes above the highest high of the preceding lookback; the trigger bar is excluded from the channel.
formula: channel = bars with opens in [t − 15m − L, t − 15m) (the L/15m bars before the trigger)
prior_high = max(high over channel)
event ⇔ close(trigger) > prior_high (strict)

terms.name: quiet_range
terms.title: Quiet range
terms.summary: Rolling state sampled at every 15m close: the trailing window range is small relative to the close.
formula: at each 15m close s: W = bars with opens in [s − window, s)
width = max(high over W) − min(low over W)
state(s) ⇔ width ≤ width_max × close(s)

terms.name: held
terms.title: Held for
terms.summary: Duration operator on a state: the state was true at every 15m sample from t − D through t.
formula: samples s = t − D, t − D + 15m, …, t on the UTC 15m grid (D/15m + 1 samples; 48h → 193)
held ⇔ state(s) is true at every sample
any known false sample → false; otherwise any absent or unknown sample → unknown
grid coverage is checked by timestamp, never by adjacent array elements

terms.name: range_contained
terms.title: Single-window containment
terms.summary: One trailing window envelope; no held timer. A contrast to held(quiet_range(…), for: …).
formula: W = bars with opens in [t − over, t)
envelope = max(high over W) − min(low over W)
true ⇔ envelope ≤ width_max × close(t)

terms.name: weekday
terms.title: Session weekday
terms.summary: The stored weekday of the calendar session on the anchor’s New York date; closed when that date has no session.
formula: New York date of the anchor instant, using the pinned session table (local day = [open − 9h30m, open + 14h30m) of that session)
value = stored weekday of that date’s session (mon … fri); closed if the date is covered but has no session

terms.name: session_tail
terms.title: Session tail
terms.summary: The anchor (bar close) falls in the half-open tail (session_end − D, session_end] of a session.
formula: true ⇔ some session close c satisfies c − D < t ≤ c
with 15m bars and a 16:00 close: last: 30m admits closes 15:45 and 16:00, not 15:30; last: 1h admits 15:15–16:00
a 30–60 minute band is session_tail(cal, last: 1h) and not session_tail(cal, last: 30m)

terms.name: completed_trend
terms.title: Completed higher-timeframe trend
terms.summary: Close versus open of the most recent expected UTC-aligned bar of the frame that ended by t.
formula: E = floor(t / frame) × frame (UTC-aligned end ≤ t); the frame bar covers [E − frame, E)
up if close(last constituent) > open(first constituent); down if <; flat if =
every constituent 15m bar must be present; no fallback to an older frame bar

terms.name: close_return
terms.title: Close return
terms.summary: Observed return from the anchor close to the close exactly h later. Each horizon is a column.
formula: r(h) = C(t + h) / C(t) − 1, where C(x) is the close of the bar that closes exactly at x
t + h after the recording end → censored; bar absent inside the recording → unknown
occurrences stay in the table when an outcome is missing; summaries use observed values only
